findings.hypothesis: Every unchanged configured workspace cycle performs three full sync-local storage writes and repeated whole-model validation, cloning and serialization.
findings.whyReachable: Startup, saved-workspace/appearance/native hints and the configured 30-second alarm call cycle. All three writes at lines 94, 97 and 120 are unconditional even when there is no edit, remote difference or appearance patch.
findings.expectedScope: CONFIRMED synthetic operation counts only. Stable synthetic 1000-entry model: 3 writes with 1158924 serialized storage bytes per cycle; complete storage contents and remote model unchanged, zero exchanges. Probe observed 24109 JSON.stringify calls and 4401830 returned characters including three fixture-side storage serializations. Empty-entry case still writes 6720 serialized bytes. Browser IPC, physical disk bytes, CPU time and RSS not measured.
findings.risk: Medium. First capture is crash recovery, merged capture preserves remote edits, final baseline avoids replay. Skipping these indiscriminately can lose changes or cause repeat uploads. Native TriggerRefresh must remain effective.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/native-and-sync-probe.mjs; noOpCycles uses actual WorkspaceSync with cloned in-memory storage and a fake local native bridge. It warms two cycles then asserts a third cycle leaves all data byte-equivalent.
findings.smallestFix: Skip sync-local writes when their persisted value is unchanged, while retaining changed pre-transport and merged captures before any failing exchange/apply. First verify no-edit, edit, remote edit, failed exchange and failed appearance paths. Further reduce repeated validation only with an internal validated-model contract while keeping external boundary validation.

findings.hypothesis: Folder expansion restoration performs a linear search of each local space pinned list for each remote folder, yielding quadratic comparison counts for many folders.
findings.whyReachable: Every configured reconciliation calls materializeWorkspace; it restores local open flags by searching localStore.spaces[*].pinned for each folder. Current model accepts the synthetic 1000-folder input within its bounds.
findings.expectedScope: CONFIRMED synthetic algorithmic count from executing production materializeWorkspace. 100 folders: 5050 predicate calls; 1000 folders: 500500. No timing benchmark or whole-browser claim. Few-folder workspaces have small costs.
findings.risk: Low to medium. A lookup map must preserve semantics for duplicate folder IDs across spaces, where the current loop lets the last matching space win, and must preserve local expansion values.
findings.cheapReproduction: Same probe, folderLookups. An own find wrapper counts calls to the unchanged production predicate and delegates to Array.prototype.find; asserts n*(n+1)/2.
findings.smallestFix: Build one map of local folder ID to expansion state in space order before materializing folders, then perform one lookup per remote folder. Preserve last-space winner and existing fallback open=true.

findings.hypothesis: Disposing while a cycle is awaiting the bridge can leave a recreated repeating alarm after disposal.
findings.whyReachable: dispose clears the alarm and listeners but drain does not recheck disposed after await sync.cycle. A later workspaceOff or reconciled result unconditionally calls alarms.create.
findings.expectedScope: CONFIRMED synthetic scheduling race with production installer: pending bridge read, dispose, then workspaceOff callback yields alarm clear followed by alarm create at 0.5 minutes. Actual Chrome worker wake cost and production dispose call frequency not measured.
findings.risk: Low. A post-await disposed guard must preserve finally resetting running. Alarm API sequencing should ensure teardown is the last alarm mutation.
findings.cheapReproduction: Same probe, disposeRace. Fake extension event/alarms APIs record calls; fake native callback is deliberately delayed until after dispose. Real 250 ms scheduling debounce runs; no network.
findings.smallestFix: After sync.cycle returns, stop before changing alarms if disposed. Test dispose during configured/off/disabled cycles and a pending alarms.create, so asynchronous alarm changes cannot overtake final cleanup.

findings.hypothesis: ReadObject copies the complete successful ciphertext vector into OpaqueSyncVaultObject instead of transferring ownership from the consumed reply.
findings.whyReachable: Successful provider object reads bind success as const and return *success.data by value while the response still owns it. This is a full std::vector copy under the expected upstream API types.
findings.expectedScope: SUSPECTED native transient allocation per read; source suggests one object-sized duplicate. No compilation, concrete upstream type confirmation, provider runtime, allocation measurement or steady-state footprint proof performed. No gain claimed.
findings.risk: Medium. Moving requires confirming generated success/response types and exclusive ownership and keeping revision/size/error checks intact.
findings.cheapReproduction: Next allowed native build: exercise an isolated fake Service response with a large bounded ciphertext vector, count allocations or compare the data pointer before/after conversion, and test all malformed response branches. Do not use a real vault.
findings.smallestFix: After verifying concrete API ownership types, bind success mutably and move validated data/revision out of the local response, with unchanged checks.
relevantExistingTests: Native transport C++ coverage needs a new isolated fake-service test; JS provider tests do not prove C++ ownership.
